articles.title: Cyclone Arnab makes landfall on the Andhra Pradesh–Yanam coast (28 Oct) — Geography / Disaster Management
articles.text:
- **Exam angle:** Bay of Bengal cyclones peak in the post-monsoon season (Oct–Dec) and the east coast bears most of the damage. Evacuation counts and shelter numbers show how the NDMA/SDMA model works. The tie-in is IMD's cyclone classification and naming under the WMO/ESCAP Panel.
- **Key facts:** Crossed the AP–Yanam coast near Narsapur on 28 Oct with sustained winds of 125–135 kmph, gusting to 150 kmph (the "very severe cyclonic storm" band). More than 84,000 people were evacuated to about 290 shelters; 3 deaths reported (press figures). Flagged for verification: "Arnab" is, to my knowledge, the Bangladesh-proposed name in the WMO/ESCAP list.
- **Notebook:** GS1 Geography (and GS3 Disaster Management).
- **Static anchor:** Savindra Singh / NCERT Class XI *Fundamentals of Physical Geography*, "Tropical Cyclones" chapter. Add this cyclone as a case study (landfall site, wind band, evacuation numbers) and cross-link it to the NDMA cyclone guidelines.

articles.title: Kuno: a 19-month-old cheetah dies of suspected shotgun injuries; poaching probe ordered — Environment
articles.text:
- **Exam angle:** This is the first reported cheetah death at Kuno from suspected shooting (as opposed to disease or intra-species injury), so it bears on human–wildlife conflict and on how well Project Cheetah is run outside the park. An SIT has been formed, and the NTCA and WCCB sent a team.
- **Key facts:** Five pellets were recovered from the body (27 Oct). The animal is reported to be a cub of the female Nirva, found near Morena/Sheopur. The cheetah was declared extinct in India in 1952. Project Cheetah began at Kuno on 17 Sep 2022 with Namibian cheetahs, followed by South African cheetahs in Feb 2023. Reports differ on the animal's sex and on its ID (KNG22), so don't memorize either.
- **Notebook:** GS3 Environment (conservation).
- **Static anchor:** Shankar IAS, "Species in News" and the Wildlife Protection Act 1972 (NTCA is a statutory body). Add a line under Project Cheetah: "first suspected poaching mortality, Oct 2026".

articles.title: Cabinet approves PM Viksit Gram Swaraj Yojana, ₹7,395.55 crore for 2026-27 to 2030-31 — Polity & Governance (Schemes)
articles.text:
- **Exam angle:** A Centrally Sponsored Scheme for Panchayati Raj capacity-building and Gram Panchayat planning (the earlier flagship was the Rashtriya Gram Swaraj Abhiyan, RGSA, restructured in 2022 — treat the successor link as likely, not confirmed). Mains line: deepening of the 73rd Amendment through *functions, funds and functionaries*.
- **Key facts:** Centre ₹4,869.48 cr and States ₹2,526.07 cr. About 2.55 lakh Gram Panchayat plans a year. About 32 lakh elected representatives to benefit. PANCHAM platform in 17 languages (these numbers come from a single aggregator, so flag them).
- **Notebook:** GS2 Polity/Governance.
- **Static anchor:** Laxmikanth, "Panchayati Raj" chapter (Part IX, Arts. 243–243O; Eleventh Schedule). Update the scheme list and cross-link it to GPDP / People's Plan Campaign.

articles.title: India and Mexico sign Terms of Reference to launch Preferential Trade Agreement (PTA) talks — International Relations / Economy
articles.text:
- **Exam angle:** India is seeking a limited-scope PTA after Mexico raised tariffs sharply (reported at up to 50%) on goods from countries with no FTA with it. A PTA covers only a negotiated list of tariff lines, which makes it narrower than an FTA, CECA or CEPA. Sectors cited: autos, pharma, electronics, critical minerals.
- **Key facts:** Signing reported on 27-28 Oct (earlier press said "likely"; confirm via MEA/Commerce Ministry when you can). Mexico belongs to USMCA. India–EFTA TEPA (Iceland, Liechtenstein, Norway, Switzerland) came into force on 1 Oct 2025, with a USD 100 bn FDI target over 15 years.
- **Notebook:** GS2 IR (Latin America) and GS3 Economy (external sector).
- **Static anchor:** Mrunal, "Trade agreements: PTA vs FTA vs CEPA". Add Mexico to the "India's Latin America engagement" map notes (with Brazil, Argentina, Chile, Peru).

articles.title: IIP grows 6.7% in September 2026 (revised base 2022-23); mining contracts — Economy
articles.text:
- **Exam angle:** IIP is a lead indicator of the industrial cycle. The revised base year (2022-23) and the use-based split show capital-goods and intermediate-goods demand.
- **Key facts:** Overall 6.7% y/y (August: 8.0%; July: 6.7%). Manufacturing 7.6%, electricity 11.2%, mining −6.2%. Capital goods 10.4%, intermediate goods 12.2%. Only the August and July figures were confirmed against a second source, so treat the September breakdown as single-source.
- **Notebook:** GS3 Economy.
- **Static anchor:** Ramesh Singh, "Industry and Infrastructure" / "Indices". Update the IIP row with base 2022-23 and the Sept 2026 print. Cross-link to the Core-industries note from 23 Oct.

articles.title: Ministry of Environment, Forest & Climate Change: India's National Statement at CBD COP-17, Yerevan (27 Oct 2026) — GS3 Environment
articles.text:
Union Environment Minister Bhupender Yadav delivered India's statement at the High-Level Segment of the 17th Conference of Parties to the Convention on Biological Diversity. India pressed for "sufficient and predictable" finance, technology transfer and capacity-building for implementing the Kunming–Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework (KMGBF), backed a multilateral benefit-sharing mechanism including the **Cali Fund** for digital sequence information (DSI), and favoured a science-based, precautionary approach to synthetic biology and biosafety.
- Figures cited: updated NBSAP with 23 National Biodiversity Targets and 142 indicators; 1,134 Protected Areas; 103 Ramsar sites; 57 Biodiversity Heritage Sites; 18 Biosphere Reserves (13 in UNESCO's MAB network); International Big Cat Alliance covers seven big-cat species.
- Programmes showcased: Mission LiFE, Ek Ped Maa Ke Naam, MISHTI, Amrit Dharohar, Soil Health Card.
- *Update note:* Ramsar count of 103 was first covered on 16 Oct; new here is the COP-17 negotiating position. (One secondary report also lists publications released at COP-17, e.g. I-OECM Guidelines 2026; not verified, so omitted.)

articles.title: Ministry of Statistics & Programme Implementation: Quick Estimates of IIP, September 2026 (28 Oct) — GS3 Economy
articles.text: Base 2022-23=100. Overall IIP growth **6.7% y/y** (index 124.3 vs 116.5 in Sept 2025), down from 8.0% in August. Manufacturing +7.6% (17 of 23 industry groups positive); Electricity & Gas +11.2%; Mining & Quarrying **-6.2%**. Estimates are quick estimates, subject to revision. Useful for the "industrial growth/indicators" theme; note the new base-year series.

articles.title: Ministry of Commerce & Industry (DPIIT): National Startup Awards 6.0 — applications open 27 Oct–20 Nov 2026 — GS3 Economy
articles.text: 20 sectoral + 3 special categories (Women-Led, North-East, first-ever Student Innovator/Aspiring Entrepreneur award); 12 new sectors incl. Biomanufacturing, Defence & Security, Electronics & Semiconductors, Ocean & Blue Economy, Space-Tech/Drones, Rural Economy. ₹25 lakh per winning startup per category. Context: Startup India launched 16 Jan 2016 (National Startup Day); Fund of Funds for Startups ₹10,000 crore (SIDBI); Startup India Seed Fund Scheme (2021).

articles.title: Ministry of Health & Family Welfare: Tobacco-Free Youth Campaign 4.0 launched (60 days) (reported 28 Oct) — GS2 Governance/Health *(single secondary source; confirm on pib.gov.in)*
articles.text:
Time-bound campaign targeting educational institutions and villages; earlier editions reportedly led to 5.8 lakh+ institutions and 73,000+ villages being declared tobacco-free. Link with COTPA 2003 and the National Tobacco Control Programme for static revision.

### Scheme-in-focus: Atal Vayo Abhyuday Yojana (AVYAY)
- **Ministry:** Social Justice & Empowerment. **Objective:** dignity, health, care and productive engagement of senior citizens.
- **Key features:** grants to NGOs/States for homes and day-care; free assistive devices (RVY); Elderline 14567; startups and jobs via SAGE/SCOPE; caregiver training (PM-SPECIAL).
- **Beneficiaries:** senior citizens (60+), with device support for BPL/≤₹15,000 monthly income.
- **Significance:** demographic ageing response (~23 crore elderly by 2036), links to Art. 41 DPSP and Maintenance of Parents Act 2007.

### Also worth a line (not verified from PIB text; secondary sources)
54th PRAGATI meeting (reviewed projects worth over ₹16,000 crore across 31 States/UTs; stress on API production in Bulk Drug Parks); India–Mexico Terms of Reference for a Preferential Trade Agreement; PLI Textiles Round 4 applications 1 Nov–31 Dec; 12th Sujal Gram Samvad (Jal Shakti, JJM 2.0, Punah Bharan app); NPPA revised MRPs for 543 anti-cancer brands from 9 Nov; BRESE 2026 with 9th ISA Assembly, 2–5 Nov.

articles.title: Cabinet clears ₹10,000 crore Container Manufacturing Promotion Scheme — Economy
articles.text:
**Exam angle:** India depends heavily on imported shipping containers; the scheme links manufacturing policy (Make in India) to maritime logistics and the Sagarmala/Maritime Amrit Kaal agenda. Mains hook: import substitution, supply-chain resilience and freight-cost competitiveness.
**Key facts:** Approved by the Union Cabinet on 28 Oct 2026 · outlay ₹10,000 crore, up to FY 2039–40 · target ~7.5 lakh TEU/year (about 10x current capacity) · >53,000 jobs expected · components reported: interest subvention, testing and certification support, land-leasing support, opex assistance. *Also cleared the same day:* 3% DA/DR hike from 1 Jul 2026; Khelo India Sports Goods Manufacturing Scheme (₹1,856 crore, 2026–27 to 2033–34); PM Viksit Gram Swaraj Yojana (₹7,395 crore, 2026–27 to 2030–31, centrally sponsored, ~2.78 lakh rural local bodies). *Flag:* the earlier August proposal was described as a five-year scheme; the approved version runs to FY 2039–40 (media reports differ slightly on structure, so check the PIB release).
**Notebook:** GS3 Economy (Manufacturing / Infrastructure — Ports).
**Static anchor:** Ramesh Singh, Infrastructure chapter (Ports, Sagarmala) + Mrunal, Industry/Trade pillar. *Nudge:* add a "container manufacturing" bullet under Make in India sectors and cross-link to the Vadhavan port note.

articles.title: Ashoke Sen becomes the first Indian physicist to receive the Oskar Klein Medal — Science & Technology
articles.text:
**Exam angle:** Relevant to Physics optional (string theory, dualities, black-hole entropy) and to "Indian scientists in news" in Prelims.
**Key facts:** Received 22 Oct 2026 at Stockholm; awarded by Stockholm University with the Nobel Committee for Physics · lecture: "Gravity from Strings and Strings from Gravity" · Sen: ICTS-Infosys Madhava Chair Professor, ICTS Bengaluru · work: S-duality, black hole entropy, string field theory · earlier: Breakthrough Prize (2012), Dirac Medal (2014).
**Notebook:** GS3 Sci-Tech (Achievements of Indians) + Physics optional (quantum gravity / string theory).
**Static anchor:** Spectrum, Science & Tech — Indian scientists; Physics optional notes on string theory. *Nudge:* add a one-line "S-duality = strong↔weak coupling equivalence" memory hook.

articles.title: Cheer pheasant: Himachal's conservation breeding shows survival rising from 11% to 100% — Environment
articles.text:
**Exam angle:** A case study in ex-situ conservation with soft release and radio/camera-trap monitoring; the species is Schedule I (WPA 1972) and IUCN Vulnerable. Useful Mains example for "successful species recovery".
**Key facts:** Survival of released birds 11.11% (2019–20) → 100% (2024–25) · Khadiyun Breeding Centre, Chail (Solan) has released 77 birds · 12 birds soft-released near Koti, Shimla (Wildlife Week, Oct 2026) · no release in 2025–26 (consolidation year) · threats: grassland fires, grazing, hunting.
**Notebook:** GS3 Environment (Biodiversity — Conservation).
**Static anchor:** Shankar IAS, Environment — ex-situ conservation and species in news. *Nudge:* add cheer pheasant to the "Himalayan galliformes" list (Western Tragopan, Monal) with status tags.

articles.title: Supreme Court (27 Oct) asks Union to revisit acid-sale guidelines, flags rising attacks as policy failure — Society
articles.text:
**Exam angle:** Bench remarks reported from the 27 Oct court round-up; no final holding yet (the matter has been pending in a PIL since earlier this year, when the Court asked the Centre about curbing or banning retail sale). Links gender-based violence, State-subject regulation and enforcement gaps.
**Key facts:** Laxmi v. UoI (2013): curbs on over-the-counter sale, ID and register; minimum compensation ₹3 lakh · Model Poisons Possession and Sale Rules, 2013 under the Poisons Act, 1919 (States to frame own rules) · BNS s.124 (min 10 years to life) · NCRB: 207 reported cases in 2023, 703 pending, only 16 convictions that year.
**Notebook:** GS1 Society (Women) / GS2 Governance.
**Static anchor:** Laxmikanth, Ch. on Fundamental Rights (Art. 21) + Shankar IAS, Women issues. *Nudge:* add the Laxmi case to the Art. 21 judgments table.

articles.title: Cabinet: Container Manufacturing Promotion Scheme (CMPS) — Rs 10,000 crore
articles.text:
**Ministry:** Ministry of Ports, Shipping & Waterways (inferred; announced in Union Budget 2026-27) | **Notebook:** GS3 Economy / Infrastructure & Industry

**What & why:** A long-duration support scheme (up to FY 2039-40) to build a domestic shipping-container manufacturing base. Global production is highly concentrated (about 95% in one country, per the Minister), so the scheme targets import dependence and supply-chain resilience, and aims to make India an export hub.

**Key facts**
- Outlay Rs 10,000 crore; runs up to FY 2039-40.
- Target: raise annual capacity nearly 10x, to 7.5 lakh TEUs.
- Components: Interest Subvention Assistance (3% p.a. on eligible term loans for greenfield/brownfield units; Rs 859 crore); Operational Expenditure Assistance for containers built to global standards (Rs 8,891 crore); testing & certification support incl. common facilities (Rs 150 crore). *(Reported component figures sum to Rs 9,900 crore; one outlet also mentions land-leasing support — check PIB text for the exact split.)*
- Jobs: ~3,000 direct, 50,000+ indirect (53,000+).

### Scheme-in-focus: Container Manufacturing Promotion Scheme
- **Objective:** Competitive domestic container industry; cut import dependence.
- **Features:** 3% interest subvention; opex assistance to bridge cost gap; common testing/certification; Budget 2026-27 announcement.
- **Beneficiaries:** Eligible container manufacturers (greenfield & brownfield), ancillary industry (corner castings, specialised steel, wooden frames, paints).
- **Significance:** Maritime self-reliance, logistics cost, Atmanirbhar Bharat; links to Maritime Amrit Kaal themes.

articles.title: Cabinet: Pradhan Mantri Viksit Gram Swaraj Yojana (PM-VGSY) — Rs 7,395.55 crore
articles.text:
**Ministry:** Ministry of Panchayati Raj (inferred) | **Notebook:** GS2 Governance / Polity (Local Government)

**What & why:** A Centrally Sponsored Scheme for 2026-27 to 2030-31 (co-terminus with the Sixteenth Finance Commission period) to make Panchayats self-reliant, accountable, high-performing institutions. Extends to all States/UTs including traditional local bodies in non-Part IX areas.

**Key facts**
- Outlay Rs 7,395.55 crore: Centre Rs 4,869.48 crore, States Rs 2,526.07 crore.
- Covers ~2.55 lakh Panchayats/traditional bodies; capacity building for ~32 lakh elected representatives and functionaries.
- Annual targets: ~2.55 lakh Gram Panchayat Development Plans (GPDPs) on eGramSwaraj; ~2.55 lakh online audit plans on AuditOnline; 1 crore+ citizens per awareness exercise.
- Digital: common platform on e-Panchayat systems; PANCHAM AI platform (17 languages) reported.
- No permanent posts; need-based contractual staff. States submit annual action plans, appraised by a Central Empowered Committee.
- Context: 16th FC recommends ~Rs 4.35 lakh crore grants for rural local bodies (2026-31).

### Scheme-in-focus: PM-VGSY
- **Objective:** Self-reliant, accountable Panchayats in line with Viksit Bharat.
- **Features:** Evidence-based GPDPs; awareness & capacity building; online audit, accounting, Own Source Revenue mobilisation; coverage of non-Part IX areas.
- **Beneficiaries:** ~2.55 lakh local bodies; ~32 lakh representatives/functionaries.
- **Significance:** Operationalises 73rd Amendment / Part IX, Finance Commission grant utilisation; fiscal decentralisation. *(Relationship to the earlier RGSA is not stated in sources read.)*

articles.title: Cabinet: Khelo India Sports Goods Manufacturing Scheme — Rs 1,856.67 crore
articles.text:
**Ministry:** Ministry of Youth Affairs & Sports (inferred), with MSDE for skilling | **Notebook:** GS3 Economy (Manufacturing) / GS2 Sports policy

**What & why:** 2026-27 to 2033-34 scheme to make India a global hub for quality sports goods, cutting import dependence and raising domestic value addition.

**Key facts**
- Components: Sports Goods Manufacturing Zones (SGMZs) built on the BHAVYA scheme and NICDC industrial parks; Anchor Investment Support and Turnover-Linked Support (about Rs 1,130 crore combined); cluster upgradation for MSMEs; International Sports Federation certification support (Rs 105 crore); Centres of Excellence and R&D linked to Anusandhan National Research Foundation; skilling with MSDE; branding via Export Promotion Mission.
- Aligned with Khelo Bharat Niti 2025, Make in India. No numerical output/job targets stated in sources read.
- Sports-goods clusters such as Jalandhar and Ludhiana flagged as beneficiaries (Tribune).

articles.title: Cabinet: Dearness Allowance / Dearness Relief raised by 3 percentage points
articles.text:
**Ministry:** Ministry of Finance (Dept. of Expenditure) | **Notebook:** GS3 Economy (Public Finance) | *Verified on PIB release, 28 Oct 2026*

- DA/DR rises from 60% to 63% of Basic Pay/Pension, effective 1 July 2026.
- Beneficiaries: ~48.54 lakh Central Government employees, ~68.71 lakh pensioners.
- Annual exchequer impact: Rs 10,016.10 crore (DA + DR combined).
- Rationale: compensate for price rise under the accepted formula based on 7th CPC recommendations.

articles.title: Jaishankar flags the Global South's "4F crisis" — International Relations
articles.text:
**Headline:** EAM says the Global South faces shortages of finance, fuel, food and fertiliser and urges the Global North to see its "equal stake" (New Delhi, 25 Oct).
**Exam angle:** Fits India's "voice of the Global South" positioning. He tied the crisis to the wars in Ukraine and West Asia, chokepoints and trade restrictions. He also called for "de-risking" and diversified options, UN reform, and AI that is not controlled by a few actors. Useful Mains line for IR questions on Global South leadership and the reform of global institutions.
**Memorise:** 4F = Finance, Fuel, Food, Fertiliser. Spoken at the Chinmaya Amrit Mahotsav Global Sammelan, Bharat Mandapam, on UN Day.
**Notebook:** GS2 International Relations.
**Static anchor:** Shankar IAS / Mrunal IR pillar "India and the Global South (Voice of Global South Summits, G20 African Union entry)". *Nudge:* add a "4F crisis" box with chokepoints (Hormuz, Red Sea, Black Sea) and cross-link to the food-security and fertiliser-subsidy notes.

articles.title: IMD–IITM study: India's climate zones are shifting; Victoria Mode implicated — Geography
articles.text:
**Headline:** A MAUSAM study redraws India's climate map over 30-year blocks (1951–80 to 1991–2020) and finds the Northeast and Gangetic West Bengal moving out of the tropical zone.
**Exam angle:** Climate classification, regional rainfall variability and food-security links. The study blames rising maximum temperatures and the Victoria Mode (a North Pacific sea-surface temperature pattern) for reduced Gangetic-plain rainfall, and recommends including ocean modes in agricultural planning. Good for a "climate change impact on Indian agriculture" Mains answer.
**Memorise:** Northeast tropical savannah ~18% to ~12% of the region; temperate zone now above 80%; Gangetic West Bengal now temperate. Authors: IMD and IITM Pune.
**Notebook:** GS1 Geography (climatology); GS3 Agriculture.
**Static anchor:** NCERT Class XI *India: Physical Environment*, Climate chapter; Spectrum/Majid Husain on Köppen types (Aw, Cwg, BSh). *Nudge:* add the study as a case for "shifting climate zones" and cross-link to ENSO/IOD notes.

articles.title: AATAL: MoES opens a source-apportionment lab for Delhi-NCR air — Science & Technology
articles.text:
**Headline:** The Integrated Atmospheric Chemistry and Aerosol Toxicity Analysis Laboratory, billed as a world first, was inaugurated at IITM's Delhi branch on 24 Oct, ahead of smog season.
**Exam angle:** Moves air-quality policy from modelled to measurement-based source identification (vehicles, industry, biomass and crop burning, dust, transported pollution) and feeds evidence to CAQM and GRAP. It links to IITM's AIRWISE decision-support system and sits under Mission Mausam.
**Memorise:** MoES; IITM Delhi branch; Mission Mausam; reported cost Rs 80 crore; inaugurated by MoS (IC) Jitendra Singh.
**Notebook:** GS3 Science & Technology / Environment (pollution).
**Static anchor:** Shankar IAS, "Environmental Pollution" (air quality, NCAP, GRAP, CAQM); Spectrum, science institutions. *Nudge:* add AATAL under "Delhi air pollution: institutions" and cross-link Mission Mausam.

articles.title: Siang Upper Multipurpose Project: protests turn violent in Pasighat — Environment
articles.text:
**Headline:** The proposed 11,200 MW NHPC project on the Siang in Arunachal Pradesh saw the NHPC office and a police station set ablaze on 23 Oct after a bandh.
**Exam angle:** A classic development-versus-displacement and ecology case: protesters cite loss of ancestral land, seismicity and ecological damage, and complain of inadequate consultation on the pre-feasibility survey. The government frames it as a strategic answer to China's proposed Medog project on the Yarlung Tsangpo, with flood-regulation and water-security benefits. Good for a Mains question on large dams, federalism and transboundary rivers.
**Memorise:** 11,200 MW; proponent NHPC; Siang = Brahmaputra's course in Arunachal Pradesh; counter to Medog (China).
**Notebook:** GS3 Environment; GS2 IR (India–China water); GS1 Geography (Places in News).
**Static anchor:** Shankar IAS, "EIA and Environmental Clearances"; Spectrum/NCERT on Brahmaputra drainage. *Nudge:* add a "Siang vs Medog" box and cross-link to Indus Waters Treaty and Brahmaputra data-sharing MoUs.

articles.title: Department of Science & Technology — Technology Development Board (TDB): ₹116 crore RDI Fund support to Manastu Space for indigenous green propulsion (26 Oct 2026)
articles.text:
**What it is / why it matters:** TDB, a statutory body under DST, signed an agreement with Navi Mumbai-based Manastu Space Technologies to support a hydrogen-peroxide-based "green" propulsion system for satellites and launch vehicles. It is among the early deployments of the **Research, Development and Innovation (RDI) Fund** for private deep-tech.

**Key facts:**
- Support: **₹116 crore** from the RDI Fund as **optionally convertible debt**; total project cost **₹277.63 crore**.
- Aim: mature the technology from **TRL-6 to TRL-9**; thrust range from **5 mN to 300 N**.
- Tech: hydrogen-peroxide-based propellant with additives, integrated engine and catalyst system; deliverables include the propulsion engine, propellant feed system and high-temperature ceramic catalysts. Claimed to be safer and cheaper than conventional (toxic hydrazine-type) propellants.
- Context: the RDI Fund is described by Minister Jitendra Singh as a ₹1 lakh crore initiative alongside the National Research Foundation.

**Notebook:** GS3 Science & Tech (space, R&D financing, startups).

articles.title: Ministry of Road Transport & Highways (MoRTH): Central Motor Vehicles Rules, 1989 amended to permit E85/E100 flex-fuel vehicles (G.S.R. 911(E) dated 23 Oct; published 26 Oct 2026) *(single trade-press source for the final notification; draft of 27 Apr 2026 verified separately)*
articles.text:
**What it is / why it matters:** The amendment extends emission/testing provisions (Rule 115) that referred to E85 so they cover **E85 or E100**. It is a regulatory step toward higher ethanol use, linked to crude-import dependence.

**Key facts:**
- E20 = 20% ethanol; E85 = 85% ethanol + 15% petrol; E100 = nearly pure ethanol.
- Applies only to vehicles **designed and certified** for high-ethanol fuels; existing petrol/E20 cars cannot use E100 and owners need not switch.
- Weight limit in the relevant provisions raised from **3,000 kg to 3,500 kg**.
- Does not itself create nationwide retail availability of E100. E100 has lower energy content per litre, so more litres are needed per km.
- The April draft also covered B100 biodiesel and hydrogen-CNG.

**Notebook:** GS3 Economy/Energy, Environment (biofuels; National Policy on Biofuels).

articles.title: CSIR / Office of the Principal Scientific Adviser: ESTIC 2026 (Emerging Science, Technology & Innovation Conclave) — Bharat Mandapam, 27–29 Oct 2026
articles.text:
**What it is / why it matters:** The second edition of a cross-ministerial platform linking public research with startups, industry, investors and academia; PM Modi inaugurates on 27 Oct.

**Key facts:**
- Organised by CSIR under guidance of the Office of the PSA (CSIR-NIIST is the organising partner); **13 ministries** involved.
- Theme: "Creative Minds, Catalyzing Science, Empowering Technologies"; **12 thematic areas** (semiconductors, quantum communication, AI, robotics, advanced manufacturing, synthetic biology, healthcare, energy, agri-tech, ocean technology, space).
- Nobel laureates named: Joachim Frank, Richard J. Roberts, Kostya Novoselov. Exhibition open to the public from day two.
- Minister Jitendra Singh cited growth from ~350–400 startups (2014) to over 2.3 lakh, and said 50–60% come from smaller towns (ministerial claims, not independently verified).

**Notebook:** GS3 Science & Tech (S&T ecosystem, innovation policy).

articles.title: India Meteorological Department / Ministry of Earth Sciences: Cyclonic Storm "Arnab" over the Bay of Bengal — landfall expected 28 Oct *(secondary sources; check IMD bulletins for latest)*
articles.text:
**What it is / why it matters:** The system intensified from a deep depression into a cyclonic storm on 26 Oct, forecast to cross the Andhra Pradesh–Yanam coast (between Bapatla and Visakhapatnam) by the forenoon of 28 Oct, with winds of 115–125 kmph (gusts to 140 kmph) and very heavy rain over Odisha.

**Key facts:**
- Name **"Arnab"** (Bengali for "sea/ocean") was proposed by **Bangladesh**, from the cyclone-name list adopted in April 2020 for the WMO/ESCAP Panel on Tropical Cyclones region.
- Good case study for the IMD (RSMC New Delhi) bulletin system, cyclone naming and disaster preparedness.

**Notebook:** GS1 Geography (cyclones); GS3 Disaster Management.

### Also worth a line (headline-level; not verified from PIB text)
- Defence Acquisition Council AoN worth about ₹2.12 lakh crore (~82% from Indian industry) — 26 Oct.
- MoSPI announced ASUSE 2027–28 (April 2027–March 2028) with new questions on women entrepreneurs' constraints.
- Nasscom–CAIT MoU on AI adoption and cyber-fraud awareness for traders/MSMEs (27 Oct, MoS Jitin Prasada).
- Health Ministry reviewed Special Campaign 6 (2–31 Oct): 336 central health institutions, ~₹50 lakh from scrap/auction.

articles.title: 12th BRICS Parliamentary Forum opens in New Delhi (26–27 Oct) — International Relations
articles.text:
**Exam angle:** India hosts the legislators' track of BRICS at Parliament House, chaired by Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla. Theme: "Fostering Parliaments for people-centric development"; AI and digital technology feature across four plenary sessions. It is a parliamentary-diplomacy platform that supports summit decisions, not a decision-making body.
**Memorize:** 1st forum Moscow, June 2015; 11th Brasília, June 2025 (zero tolerance on terrorism, Pahalgam condemned). Members: Brazil, Russia, India, China, South Africa, Egypt, Ethiopia, Iran, UAE, Indonesia.
**Notebook:** GS2 – International Relations.
**Static anchor:** Shankar IAS / Mrunal "Groupings" pillar – BRICS. Update: add forum dates and the 2025 terrorism language; cross-link to Parliamentary Diplomacy (Laxmikanth – Parliament, Speaker's role).

articles.title: Indian shipbuilding: order book growing, global share still tiny — Economy
articles.text:
**Exam angle:** BIMCO data show a record global order book of 203.2 million CGT, up 13% in a year and above the 2008 peak (195.4 m CGT). India holds ~1.1 m CGT (0.5%), ranking 12th, but deliveries due 2026–30 are nearly double those of 2021–25 (verify).
**Memorize:** China ~64%, South Korea ~19%, Japan ~6% of the order book; China won 74% of tonnage contracted last year. Targets: Maritime India Vision 2030 (top 10) and Maritime Amrit Kaal Vision 2047 (top 5). ₹69,725-crore 2025 package with Maritime Development Fund. CGT = compensated gross tonnage.
**Notebook:** GS3 – Economy (Infrastructure / Manufacturing).
**Static anchor:** Mrunal "Infrastructure – Ports & Shipping"; Sagarmala. Update: add the share data and the Amrit Kaal targets; cross-link to Make in India / Atmanirbhar defence shipbuilding.

articles.title: Prime Minister's Office / RBI (Ministry of Finance sphere): PM inaugurates RBI's new Data Centre and Enterprise Computing & Cybersecurity Training Institute, Bhubaneswar (25 Oct 2026)
articles.text:
**What / why it matters:** A greenfield disaster-recovery-grade data centre for the central bank, supporting currency management, payment and settlement systems and regulatory data, plus a training institute for cybersecurity and emerging technologies. It strengthens resilience of critical financial infrastructure (a recurring Mains theme) and spreads such infrastructure beyond Mumbai.

**Key facts** (project details from pre-event reports; PIB listing confirms the inauguration)
- Location: Info Valley-II, Khordha district, near Bhubaneswar, Odisha; ~18.55-acre campus; reported cost ~₹169 crore.
- Acts as a backup to RBI's primary data centre at Kharghar, Navi Mumbai; foundation stone laid 22 Mar 2023.
- Chosen partly for seismic stability and to diversify cyber/concentration risk.

**Notebook:** GS3 Economy (financial-sector infrastructure, cyber-resilience); GS3 Sci-Tech/Security (critical information infrastructure).

articles.title: India tells the UN: the Security Council has a "legitimacy deficit" — International Relations
articles.text:
- **Exam angle:** India's standing push for IGN (Intergovernmental Negotiations) reform: expansion in both categories, veto question, and the bid for a non-permanent seat in 2028–29. Mains-ready line: a Council frozen in 1945 cannot claim to speak for the 2026 world.
- **Facts to memorise:** India called the UNSC's structure a "deficit in legitimacy" and wants expansion of **both permanent and non-permanent** seats. Asia-Pacific holds **>60% of world population** but has thin Council representation. India has served **eight** non-permanent terms (latest **2021–22**) and is a candidate for **2028–29**. Obstacles: Charter amendment needs **two-thirds of the General Assembly plus ratification by two-thirds of members including all P5** (Art. 108), and opposition from the **Uniting for Consensus** group. (Reported via a daily-affairs digest; date of statement ~23–24 Oct.)
- **Notebook:** GS2 – IR (Global groupings / UN reforms).
- **Static anchor:** Shankar IAS – UN & reforms; Mrunal – G4, L.69, UfC groups. *Nudge:* add a table of G4 vs UfC vs L.69 vs African Union (Ezulwini Consensus) positions.

articles.title: Loss and Damage Fund: first-ever extraordinary Board meeting; $21.6 million set aside for Nepal after the Bhotekoshi flood — Environment
articles.text:
- **Exam angle:** Operationalising climate justice. The FRLD's first disaster-specific response sits against Nepal's estimated recovery need of ≥ **$4.71 bn**: a case for the adequacy debate before **COP31**.
- **Facts to memorise:** Trigger: ice-and-rock avalanche on **26 Aug 2026** causing a debris flow along the **Bhotekoshi–Trishuli–Narayani** system. Board virtual extraordinary meeting on **22 Oct**; provision of **$21.6 m = $20 m for Nepal + $1.6 m oversight fees**, with Nepal invited to submit a funding request (a digest reports it as "provisionally approved"). Nepal's government estimates losses ≥ $2.69 bn. FRLD was agreed at **COP27 (Sharm el-Sheikh, 2022)**, operationalised at **COP28 (Dubai, 2023)**; **World Bank** is interim trustee (hosted). **COP31: 9–22 Nov 2026, Türkiye** (per Kathmandu Post).
- **Notebook:** GS3 – Environment (climate finance, disasters).
- **Static anchor:** Shankar IAS – UNFCCC, COP timeline, Loss & Damage (Warsaw Mechanism 2013); Spectrum – Climate change. *Nudge:* extend your COP timeline with COP27 → FRLD → COP28 operationalisation → first disbursement (2026).

articles.title: ISRO's NVS-03 slated for ~30 Oct on GSLV: the push to restore NavIC — Science & Technology
articles.text:
- **Exam angle:** NavIC's reliability crisis (ageing rubidium clocks, NVS-02 failure) makes NVS-03 strategic: defence, aviation, Aadhaar-linked and fleet use. Classic UPSC space-tech terrain (NavIC was a Prelims 2018 question).
- **Facts to memorise:** Third satellite of the **second-generation NVS series**; launch vehicle **GSLV** from **Sriharikota** (date reported as 30 Oct; vehicle reported variously as GSLV Mk II/GSLV-F18, so verify on the ISRO notice). **11** NavIC satellites launched so far, **8** functional; only **3** serving navigation, **4** needed for a 3D fix. **NVS-02 (29 Jan 2025)** failed to reach intended orbit. **IRNSS-1F** lost its atomic clock after its 10-year design life. Features: indigenous rubidium clocks, **L1, L5 and S-band**, coverage up to **~1,500 km** beyond India, **SPS** (civil) and **RS** (restricted).
- **Notebook:** GS3 – Science & Technology (Space).
- **Static anchor:** Shankar/Spectrum – Space technology: navigation (GPS, GLONASS, Galileo, BeiDou, NavIC); orbits. *Nudge:* update your NavIC card with the NVS series and the 3 GEO + 4 IGSO original design.

articles.title: Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers' Welfare: India creates 11 crore Farmer IDs — five months ahead of deadline (announced 24 Oct 2026) *(UPDATE — Farmer Registry/Agri-Stack mentioned in earlier briefings; new is the target being met)*
articles.text:
**What / why it matters:** Union Agriculture Minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan announced that the target of 11 crore Farmer IDs under the **Digital Agriculture Mission** was reached by the night of 23 Oct 2026. Each farmer gets a unique, verified digital identity linked to land records, so schemes, credit and relief can be delivered without repeated document checks. This is the "farmer registry" layer of India's agricultural digital public infrastructure (DPI).

**Key facts**
- Digital Agriculture Mission: approved by the Union Cabinet on **2 Sep 2024**; builds DPI incl. a verified farmer database.
- Target reached about **five months ahead** of the deadline (ANI: 31 March 2027; one other report says Dec 2027 — treat the date as unsettled).
- Over **6 crore farmers** have already received benefits through Farmer-ID-based delivery.
- Intended uses: faster KCC/credit, crop insurance (PMFBY) and disaster relief, MSP procurement with direct bank transfers, fewer duplicate/fraudulent claims.
- States/UTs are working to include **tenant farmers/actual cultivators**; Minister called it "cooperative federalism".

**Notebook:** GS3 Agriculture / GS2 Governance (e-governance, DPI).

articles.title: Ministry of Earth Sciences (IITM): AATAL — integrated air-pollution analysis lab inaugurated in Delhi (24 Oct 2026)
articles.text:
**What / why it matters:** MoS Dr Jitendra Singh inaugurated the *Integrated Atmospheric Chemistry and Aerosol Toxicity Analysis Laboratory (AATAL)* at IITM's Delhi branch, ahead of the winter smog season. It aims to identify pollution sources in near real time and estimate each source's relative share, and to study aerosol toxicity.

**Key facts**
- Set up under **Mission Mausam** at a cost of about **₹80 crore**.
- Sources covered: vehicles, industry, biomass/crop-residue burning, construction and road dust, and transported pollution.
- Works with IITM's **AIRWISE** system (forecasts + observations + source apportionment).
- Evidence meant to support the **Commission for Air Quality Management (CAQM)** and **GRAP** planning.
- "World's first of its kind" is the Minister's claim — not independently verified.

**Notebook:** GS3 Environment / Science & Tech.

articles.title: EAM Jaishankar in Baku: India welcomes the Armenia–Azerbaijan peace agreement — International Relations
articles.text:
- **Exam angle:** India re-engages Azerbaijan, a Pakistan-leaning South Caucasus state. The visit (23 Oct) is a calibrated reset around connectivity (INSTC), energy and terrorism, and follows a Modi–Aliyev meeting at the SCO Summit in Bishkek. The MEA did not confirm that cross-border terrorism was raised.
- **Facts to memorise:** Jaishankar called on President **Ilham Aliyev** and held talks with FM **Jeyhun Bayramov**. Agreed to deepen political consultations and exchange visits. Discussed trade, investment, connectivity and energy. India "welcomed" the Armenia–Azerbaijan peace agreement. Jaishankar thanked Azerbaijan for helping evacuate Indian students from Iran during the West Asia conflict, and invited Bayramov to India. Azerbaijan recently hosted a CICA meeting (India was represented by MoS Kirti Vardhan Singh).
- **Notebook:** GS2 – IR (Eurasia / extended neighbourhood).
- **Static anchor:** Shankar IAS – India's relations with Central Asia & Caucasus; Mrunal – INSTC / connectivity. *Nudge:* add Azerbaijan to your INSTC map (India–Iran–Azerbaijan–Russia) and a Caspian-states cross-link.

articles.title: NTCA's 6th Management Effectiveness Evaluation of Tiger Reserves (MEE-TR 2026) makes solid-waste management a separate criterion — Environment
articles.text:
- **Exam angle:** Conservation governance is being measured on outcomes and ecology of waste, not just inputs. Ties to International Snow Leopard Day (23 Oct), which highlights big-cat conservation beyond tigers.
- **Facts to memorise:** Launched (inception workshop, with the Technical Manual) in late Sept 2026 by the Environment Minister; organised by **NTCA with the Wildlife Institute of India**. Covers all **58** tiger reserves. MEE began in **2006**, four-yearly; 2022 (5th cycle) covered 51 reserves with **Periyar** first (94.38%). Bands: Excellent ≥90%, Very Good 75–89%, Good 60–74%, Fair 50–59%. New in 2026: mandatory **solid waste management** criterion (forest posts, tourism zones, rescue centres, biomedical waste); more remote-sensing / geo-tagged patrol evidence; community and sociology experts on evaluation teams. Framework adapted from the IUCN-WCPA framework. Snow leopard: 718 (SPAI, WII), Ladakh 477; CITES Appendix I.
- **Notebook:** GS3 – Environment / Biodiversity.
- **Static anchor:** Shankar IAS – Protected Area Network, Project Tiger & NTCA; Spectrum – Wildlife conservation. *Nudge:* update the MEE-TR cycle timeline and cross-link to the Wildlife (Protection) Act 1972 (2006 amendment).

articles.title: Ministry of Law & Justice (23rd Law Commission of India): National Conference on Co-operative Federalism and Law Reforms, New Delhi (inaugurated by Vice-President C.P. Radhakrishnan; ~22 Oct 2026)
articles.text:
**What & why it matters:** The Law Commission convened State Law Commissions, jurists, former judges, Bar and academia to strengthen coordination between the Centre and States on law reform while respecting State autonomy — relevant to the Concurrent List, uniform vs. regional laws, and the Commission's advisory role.

**Key facts:** Organised by the 23rd Law Commission; Union Law & Justice Minister Arjun Ram Meghwal present; themes — law reforms, co-operative federalism, constitutional governance, institutional frameworks for administration of justice. The Law Commission is a **non-statutory, executive-constituted advisory body** (constituted for fixed terms by the Government via gazette notification). The exact conference date was inferred from a 21 Oct pre-announcement ("tomorrow") and the VP Secretariat's 22 Oct release (secondary source for details).

**Notebook:** GS2 — Polity/Governance (federalism; judiciary & law reform).

articles.title: Three Indian sites added to UNESCO's World Heritage Tentative List (20 Oct) — Art & Culture / Geography
articles.text:
**Exam angle:** Tentative List entry is the mandatory first step before a World Heritage nomination. The additions pair two rare geological sites with an early-medieval archaeological landscape, a useful "Places in News" cluster.
**Key facts:**
- Karst–Mud-Volcano Complex of Baratang (Baratang Island, Andaman): limestone caves and mud volcanoes.
- Andaman Subduction Volcanoes: Narcondam and Barren Island (India's only active volcano).
- Sirpur Cultural and Archaeological Landscape, Chhattisgarh.
- Reported totals: 81 sites on the Tentative List; 45 World Heritage Sites after Sarnath's inscription in July 2026 (secondary sources; verify before quoting).
**Notebook:** GS1 Art & Culture / Geography.
**Static anchor:** Nitin Singhania, *Art & Culture* (UNESCO heritage chapter) and Spectrum/NCERT Geography (Andaman volcanoes, mud volcanoes). Nudge: add Baratang, Narcondam and Sirpur to your "Places in News" map and cross-link to Barren Island.

articles.title: Badr MoU: Pakistan, Türkiye, Qatar and Indonesia sign a defence-industrial accord in Doha (21 Oct) — International Relations
articles.text:
**Exam angle:** It is a cooperation memorandum on joint manufacturing, technology sharing, training and R&D, not a mutual-defence treaty. Contrast it with the August Saudi–Türkiye–Pakistan Makkah pact, which has an "attack on one is an attack on all" clause.
**Key facts:**
- Signed by the defence ministers or deputies of the four states.
- India's concerns: Pakistan could diversify away from China-dependent supply, and tech access could aid its drone programme.
- Indonesia is also in talks with India on a reported ~$630 million BrahMos/Astra deal, which adds a diplomatic wrinkle.
**Notebook:** GS2 International Relations (India's neighbourhood, West Asia).
**Static anchor:** Mrunal IR pillar "India–Pakistan / West Asia". Nudge: add a comparison table of Badr vs Makkah pact vs NATO Article 5.

articles.title: Ministry of Earth Sciences: MoES–AcSIR MoU — all 10 MoES institutes become AcSIR Associated Research Institutes for PhD programmes (signed 21 Aug 2026; announced ~13 Oct 2026)
articles.text:
- **What it is:** A partnership giving MoES research institutes a common route to run research-based PhD programmes through the Academy of Scientific and Innovative Research (AcSIR). Selected scholars research at a host MoES institute under MoES scientists recognised as AcSIR faculty; **AcSIR awards the degree** and the host institute is named on the certificate. Coordinators are appointed at institute and ministry levels.
- **Why it matters:** Builds a doctoral pipeline for weather/climate, ocean, polar, seismology and coastal sciences — supports Deep Ocean Mission, Mission Mausam and climate-science capacity.
- **Key facts:** 10 MoES institutes; participating in the latest PhD enrolment cycle; areas include weather & climate, oceans, polar regions, earthquakes, coastal processes, marine robotics and AI in earth sciences. (Seat numbers/funding not stated.)
- **Notebook:** GS3 Sci-Tech / GS2 Education (higher-education & research capacity).

articles.title: India–Poland: Modi–Tusk talks push defence, space and nuclear cooperation — International Relations
articles.text:
- **Exam angle:** Poland's PM Donald Tusk is on a three-day visit (arrived 21 Oct; Delhi 22 Oct, Bengaluru 23 Oct). Modi cited defence, space and nuclear energy and invited Polish firms to co-develop and manufacture with Indian partners. The leaders also discussed Ukraine, West Asia and reform of global governance institutions. Poland is India's gateway to Central Europe and is a frontline NATO state, so the visit also fits the India–EU outreach theme.
- **Memorize:** Ties elevated to Strategic Partnership in Aug 2024 (Modi's Warsaw visit); Tusk is accompanied by Finance & Economy Minister Andrzej Domański; India–Poland Business Forum in Delhi (22 Oct) and Bengaluru (23 Oct). No specific signed agreements were reported in the coverage I could verify.
- **Notebook:** GS2 International Relations (India and Europe).
- **Static anchor:** Mrunal/Shankar IR pillar "India–EU and Europe"; add a "Central Europe: Poland (Strategic Partnership 2024)" line and cross-link to the Operation Ganga (2022 evacuation via Poland) case study.

articles.title: China tightens export controls on tunnel-boring machines from 18 November — International Relations / Economy
articles.text:
**Exam angle:** A clean case of "weaponised interdependence": India's metro, rail and highway tunnelling depends on imported TBMs, and China is adding them to its dual-use export-licence regime just as India–China ties are being normalised post-Galwan. Good for Mains answers on supply-chain resilience, Atmanirbhar manufacturing and India–China relations.
**Key facts:**
- China's Commerce Ministry (MOFCOM) announced the change, reported by Reuters; it takes effect **18 November 2026**. Exporters will need a licence under China's export-control law and dual-use rules. The same update reportedly adjusted controls on drone-related items and dredgers.
- The Hindu's digest adds that heavy machinery used above **3,000 m** (e.g., plateau-type shotcrete machines) is covered, with licences for sensitive or disputed destinations and prior registration for others; this detail rests on one source.
- Precedent: in **Sept 2025** Germany's ambassador said Chinese customs had held at least **three Herrenknecht TBMs** bound for Indian projects; they were later released, and Herrenknecht decided to **produce in India**.

**Notebook:** GS2 – International Relations (India–China); GS3 – Economy (infrastructure, manufacturing).
**Static anchor:** Shankar IAS / Mrunal "India and its neighbourhood" – India–China; Mrunal economy pillar "Infrastructure". Add a cross-link: rare-earth and fertiliser curbs (2025) → TBM curbs (2026) as a pattern of China's export-control leverage.

articles.title: Ministry of Commerce & Industry: India–New Zealand Free Trade Agreement enters into force, 20 Oct 2026 *(UPDATE — negotiations/signing covered earlier; new is entry into force)*
articles.text:
- Signed 27 April 2026. Indian exports get duty-free access to New Zealand from day one; sensitive Indian items (dairy, sugar, edible oils, certain meat/agri goods) are excluded from India's concessions; apples, kiwifruit and Manuka honey get limited access via tariff-rate quotas/seasonal windows.
- NZ commits to facilitate **USD 20 billion** investment into India; mobility: 5,000 temporary employment entry visas, 1,000 working-holiday visas a year, and post-study work rights (up to 3 years STEM; up to 4 years doctoral).
- **Notebook:** GS2 IR; GS3 Economy (trade).

articles.title: CWC reservoir bulletin: storage at ~68.6% of live capacity across 178 major reservoirs; the South is the weak spot — Geography
articles.text:
**Exam angle:** An El Niño year plus a deficient monsoon is stressing water storage. Useful for GS1 (monsoon, water resources), GS3 (irrigation, food security) and GS2 (inter-state water disputes, e.g., Cauvery, Krishna).
**Key facts:**
- The CWC bulletin of **15 Oct 2026** (as reported by a UPSC digest; the full bulletin was not accessed) puts storage at **126.717 BCM, or 68.58%** of the usable (live) capacity of **178 reservoirs**.
- Earlier, a 24 Sept CWC update showed about **70% storage against a 10-year average of 76.62%**. **South India was at about 50%**; cumulative monsoon rainfall was about 12% below normal, and parts of Maharashtra and Karnataka were declared drought-hit.
- Reported weak spots: Aliyar, Idukki, Somasila and Mettur reservoirs; Pennar, Cauvery and Krishna basins show the largest deficits. Narmada and Mahanadi basins are above normal.
- **CWC:** under the Ministry of Jal Shakti; formed 1945 (renamed 1951); HQ New Delhi; monitors reservoir storage, issues flood forecasts, handles dam design and safety.

**Notebook:** GS1 Geography (Indian monsoon, water resources) / GS3 Agriculture (irrigation).
**Static anchor:** NCERT Class XI *India: Physical Environment* – Climate; Spectrum "Water Resources". Add today's figure to a "storage vs 10-year average" tracker and cross-link to the 15 Oct WMO El Niño note.

articles.title: Draft lab-animal rules, 2026: 3Rs, registration and Institutional Animal Ethics Committees — Environment (Animal Welfare)
articles.text:
**Exam angle:** A draft rule-making story that links the Prevention of Cruelty to Animals Act, 1960 with Article 51A(g) (compassion for living creatures). Animal-rights groups such as PETA India have asked for withdrawal, arguing it weakens oversight. Good for "Statements" MCQs on regulators and committees.
**Key facts:**
- Issued by the **Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry & Dairying** on **6 Oct 2026** as **G.S.R. 864(E)**; comments invited until **6 Nov 2026**.
- Built on the **3Rs: Replacement, Reduction, Refinement**.
- Breeders, traders and establishments register with the **CCSEA** (generally valid 3 years); experiments need prior approval of the CCSEA or the **Institutional Animal Ethics Committee (IAEC)**, which has **nine members** including a scientist, a veterinarian, an external member and a socially aware member.
- Use of protected wildlife, wild/stray animals and **non-human primates is restricted**, subject to scientific justification and permission.
- Which earlier rules it supersedes was not stated in the source I read; check the notification text before writing it into notes.

**Notebook:** GS3 Environment (animal welfare) / GS2 Governance (delegated legislation).
**Static anchor:** Shankar IAS – Environment: "Animal welfare laws"; Laxmikanth – Fundamental Duties (Art. 51A(g)). Nudge: add a table of Animal Welfare Board of India vs. the experiments committee, with legal basis for each.

articles.title: UPSC (constitutional body): Commission completes 100 years (1 Oct 1926 – 1 Oct 2026) — *PIB backgrounder, via PIB-summary sites, 19 Oct*
articles.text:
- **What / why it matters:** The Public Service Commission began on 1 Oct 1926 as an advisory body (Chairman and Members appointed in London). The Government of India Act, 1935 made consultation mandatory. On 26 Jan 1950 the Federal PSC became UPSC, an independent constitutional body under **Part XIV, Arts. 315–323**. Directly relevant to the merit-based civil service and the "steel frame" theme.
- **Key facts:** ICS exam introduced in London 1855; first held in India (Allahabad) 1922; Lee Commission (1924) recommended a statutory PSC; Kothari Committee (1979) gave the three-stage exam; Mains restructured to four GS papers in 2013; Universal Registration Number introduced May 2025; AI-based facial authentication used for CS (Prelims) on 24 May 2026 (about 5.5 lakh candidates). Women's share among recommended candidates rose from 6% (1952) to 31.2% (CSE 2025). Current Chairman: Dr Ajay Kumar (since 15 May 2025).
- **Notebook:** GS2 Governance / Polity (constitutional bodies).

articles.title: Parliament (Rajya Sabha Secretariat / Lok Sabha): India at the 153rd Inter-Parliamentary Union (IPU) Assembly, Arusha, Tanzania (early–mid Oct 2026; PIB release 19 Oct)
articles.text:
- **What / why it matters:** India's delegation was led by **Harivansh, Deputy Chairman of Rajya Sabha** (members incl. Anurag Singh Thakur, Sasmit Patra, Lata Wankhede). Assembly agenda: an emergency item on climate-related disasters (proposed by Nepal; covers the Himalayan region), a general debate on good governance and inclusivity, and panels on UN conflict-prevention machinery and AI and the future of work. Outcomes reported: **Arusha Communiqué** and resolutions on persons with disabilities and climate resilience in the Himalayas. **Milton Dick** (Speaker, Australian House of Representatives) elected the **32nd IPU President** (9 Oct).
- **Notebook:** GS2 Polity / International Relations (parliamentary diplomacy; IPU is the global organisation of national parliaments, HQ Geneva).

articles.title: India's first GLOF early warning system goes live at Ghepan Ghat lake, Lahaul & Spiti — Geography
articles.text:
**Exam angle:** A pilot system built by C-DAC and funded by NDMA was installed on Thursday (15 Oct) at a lake that ISRO flagged in November 2023 for rapid expansion. It is a concrete case study for Himalayan glacial hazards under climate change.
**Key facts:**
- Location: Ghepan Ghat glacial lake, Lahaul & Spiti, Himachal Pradesh, about 4,100 m.
- Components: buoy-based lake monitoring station, automatic weather station, glacier vision unit; all feed C-DAC's supercomputing platform for real-time alerts and GLOF scenario simulation.
- Earlier reporting put the lake's growth at about 176 per cent, with the Chandrabhaga river system draining to the Chenab downstream.
- Himachal has identified 67 vulnerable glacial lakes (larger than 10 ha); four high-risk sites are prioritised under the National Landslide Mitigation Programme.
- GLOF = sudden release of water from a glacial or moraine-dammed lake.

**Notebook:** GS1 Geography / GS3 Disaster Management
**Static anchor:** Spectrum / NCERT, Himalayan glaciers and drainage; Shankar, Disaster Management. Add this as a case study beside Chorabari (2013) and South Lhonak (2023), and cross-link to the NDMA GLOF guidelines.

articles.title: Election Commission orders Special Summary Revision of rolls in 17 States/UTs; machine-readable rolls conceded — Polity & Governance
articles.text:
**Exam angle:** After the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) controversy, the EC is running a lighter annual-style revision in poll-bound states, with a notable transparency concession on readable rolls. Useful for the "electoral reforms and EC credibility" Mains theme.
**Key facts:**
- Covers 17 States/UTs, including Assam (a special revision for legal reasons), Bihar, Gujarat, Kerala, Tamil Nadu, Uttar Pradesh and West Bengal.
- Qualifying date 1 January 2027; final rolls on 4 January 2027.
- No house-to-house BLO visits, since electors were largely identified during SIR.
- Parties get weekly addition/deletion/modification supplements; soft copies in "readable PDF" (no photos), a reversal of the earlier stand.
- Opposition demands the CEC's resignation, calling the move "too little, too late".

**Notebook:** GS2 Polity/Governance
**Static anchor:** Laxmikanth, Election Commission and Electoral Reforms (Art. 324, 326; RP Act 1950 s.14 qualifying dates). Add a one-line comparison table of SIR vs SSR.

articles.title: SC: children have a fundamental right to internet access; safety and freedom "are not at odds" — Polity & Governance
articles.text:
**Exam angle:** A bench of Justices J.B. Pardiwala and K.V. Chandran, hearing reports of paid promotion of child sexual abuse material (CSEAM) through redirect links, reportedly rejected age-based blanket restrictions on children's internet use. This extends the line of cases on the internet and Articles 19(1)(a) and 21, and it is a good Mains example of balancing rights against protection.
**Key facts:**
- The Centre must frame guidelines for national databases of perceptual hashes and URLs.
- Safeguards are required against wrongful deletion, with a grievance redressal mechanism for wrong matches.
- The databases must not be repurposed to remove other kinds of content.
- Platforms must speed up detection and removal, and close the gap where content removed on one platform is not flagged on others.
- Quote: "Our children are entitled to both" (safety and freedom).
- Reports cite Articles 21 and 19(1)(a); the case name was not given in the sources I could open.

**Notebook:** GS2 Polity/Governance
**Static anchor:** Laxmikanth, Fundamental Rights (Art. 19 and 21). Add a line for *Anuradha Bhasin* (2020), *Puttaswamy* (2017) and this order, and cross-link to the POCSO Act and IT Act s.67B.

articles.title: Ministry of Commerce & Industry (CGPDTM, DPIIT) with Ministry of Ayush: Status Report on Ayush-related inventions — filings up ~8x in a decade (16 Oct 2026)
articles.text:
- **What it is:** The Office of the Controller General of Patents, Designs & Trademarks (CGPDTM, under DPIIT) compiled FY2014-15 to FY2025-26 data on patent applications in Ayush systems. The Ministry of Ayush publicised it; PIB headline: "Ayush Innovation Sees Eightfold Rise in Patent Filings".
- **Why it matters:** Shows growing IP-awareness in traditional medicine, and links to the debate on protecting traditional knowledge (TKDL, Section 3(p) of the Patents Act, WIPO GRATK treaty).
- **Key facts:**
  - Total **4,077 applications; 711 grants** (grant rate ~17%; many recent filings still pending).
  - Annual filings rose from **63 (FY15) to 590 (FY26)** — about 836% growth. Peak: 606 in FY2022-23; dip to 299 in FY2023-24.
  - Annual grants rose from 3 (FY16) to 204 (FY24). Post-COVID years (FY21–FY26) account for ~70% of filings and ~92% of grants.
  - Applicants: natural persons 2,113 (51.9%); educational institutions 995; corporates/others 700; small entities 144; startups 125. **Maharashtra** leads (744 filings, 142 grants).
  - Related, static background: **TKDL** (CSIR) is a database of traditional-knowledge formulations used by patent offices as prior-art evidence; **Section 3(p), Patents Act 1970** bars patents on traditional knowledge/mere aggregation of known properties; **WIPO GRATK Treaty** (adopted 24 May 2024) requires patent applicants to disclose country of origin/source of genetic resources and associated traditional knowledge.
- **Notebook:** GS3 Science & Tech / IPR; GS2 Health & Governance (Ayush).

articles.title: India's Ramsar sites reach 103: Sukhna Wetland (Chandigarh) and Sauj Jheel (UP) — Environment
articles.text:
- **Exam angle:** Announced 15 Oct by Environment Minister Bhupender Yadav. A "Places in News" and wetland-conservation item.
- **Memorise:** Total 103. Sukhna = Ramsar site no. 2602, man-made reservoir (1958) on the Sukhna Choe, Shivalik foothills, Chandigarh's first Ramsar site. Sauj Jheel = no. 2603, perennial floodplain lake in Mainpuri, UP, an IBA hosting 30,000+ waterbirds; UP now has 14 sites.
- **Notebook:** GS3 Environment / GS1 Geography.
- **Static anchor:** Shankar IAS "Wetlands"; Majid Husain geography. *Update:* refresh Ramsar tally (103) and add the two sites to the map.

articles.title: Ministry of Environment, Forest & Climate Change: India's Ramsar sites rise to 103 — Sukhna Wetland (Chandigarh) and Sauj Jheel (Mainpuri, UP) added (announced 15 Oct)
articles.text:
**What / why it matters:** The Environment Minister announced two new Wetlands of International Importance under the Ramsar Convention, taking India's tally from 101 to 103. It is a standard Prelims "tally + location" item and links to wetland conservation, the Central Asian Flyway and the Wetlands (Conservation and Management) Rules.

**Key facts:**
- **Sukhna Wetland (Chandigarh)** — Ramsar Site No. 2602; man-made reservoir at the Shivalik foothills, created in 1958 by damming the seasonal Sukhna Choe; wintering/stopover site on the Central Asian Flyway. Species cited: Common Pochard (VU), Pallas's Fish Eagle (EN), Black Pond Turtle (EN). First Ramsar site of Chandigarh.
- **Sauj Jheel (Mainpuri, Uttar Pradesh)** — Ramsar Site No. 2603; perennial shallow floodplain lake in the Ganga basin, an Important Bird and Biodiversity Area; hosts 30,000+ waterbirds; habitat for Sarus Crane and Greater Spotted Eagle (both VU).
- Mainpuri becomes the only district with two Ramsar sites (other: Saman Bird Sanctuary, 2019). UP's tally reported as 14.

**Notebook:** GS3 Environment (wetlands, biodiversity conservation, international conventions).

articles.title: Ministry of Commerce & Industry: National Strategic Trade Command Centre (NSTCC) launched at Vanijya Bhawan (15 Oct)
articles.text:
**What / why it matters:** A data-analytics platform to monitor, analyse and govern India's trade ecosystem, giving a consolidated view of trade performance, export-promotion schemes, regulatory approvals, application processing and operational indicators. It supports evidence-based policy and trade facilitation.

**Key facts:**
- Launched by Commerce & Industry Minister Piyush Goyal.

articles.title: WMO: El Niño "firmly established" — Oct–Dec Niño 3.4 anomaly forecast near +3.7°C, a record — Geography
articles.text:
**Exam angle:** New sub-development on the El Niño thread (our 4 Oct item covered only the monsoon wrap-up): the forecast intensity, the role of a positive IOD, and the drier-than-normal signal over the Indian subcontinent in Oct–Dec. Great Prelims-conceptual and Mains (agriculture, rabi, inflation) material.
**Key facts:** WMO update (8 Oct 2026): El Niño likely to peak around December and persist through Feb 2027 (near-100% likelihood), potentially among the strongest since 1950. Niño 3.4 anomaly +1.6°C (June) → +2.5°C (Aug); Oct–Dec forecast ≈ +3.7°C vs previous record +2.6°C (Nov 2015–Jan 2016). Positive IOD expected to peak in October (≈ +0.5°C). Informal "super El Niño" = anomaly ≥ +2.0°C. Aug 2026 was the hottest August on record. Tamil Nadu gets ~48–50% of annual rain from the Northeast Monsoon, which El Niño often favours.
**Notebook:** GS1 Geography (climatology) / GS3 Agriculture.
**Static anchor:** NCERT Class XI Fundamental of Physical Geography — Atmospheric Circulation (ENSO, Walker cell); Savindra Singh. *Nudge:* add a Walker-circulation diagram with El Niño vs La Niña vs IOD phases, and a "Niño 3.4 thresholds" line.

articles.title: The World Circular Economy Forum opens in Gandhinagar — its 10th edition and its first in South Asia — Environment
articles.text:
**Headline.** WCEF 2026 runs **15–18 September at Mahatma Mandir, Gandhinagar**, on the theme *"Circular economy: Transition for people and prosperity"* — convened by Finland's **Sitra** with the **Central Pollution Control Board**, supported by MoEFCC and the Gujarat government. Over 2,000 participants from 65-plus countries; 125-plus exhibitors. The Board of the **10-Year Framework of Programmes on Sustainable Consumption and Production (10YFP)** meets at Gandhinagar on 15 September, with India having recently taken over as **Co-Chair**.

**Exam angle.** Circularity is the connective tissue between SDG 12, the plastics-treaty negotiations, critical-mineral security and Mission LiFE — a single Mains paragraph can carry all four. The examiner's favourite distinction is **recycling (end-of-pipe, still linear) vs circularity (design-stage: durability, repairability, reuse, remanufacture)**, and the Indian policy instrument that operationalises it is **Extended Producer Responsibility**, which UPSC has already asked about directly.

**Facts to memorise.**

- WCEF launched by **Sitra (the Finnish Innovation Fund) at Helsinki in 2017**; 2026 is the **10th edition**, the first in South Asia.
- **10YFP** — the SCP framework adopted at **Rio+20 (2012)**, secretariat with UNEP; India now Co-Chair of its Board.
- India's architecture: **NITI Aayog's 11 circular-economy committees (March 2021)** across municipal solid and liquid waste, scrap metal, Li-ion batteries, tyres and rubber, gypsum, end-of-life vehicles, e-waste, hazardous industrial waste, used oil, agricultural waste and solar panels.
- EPR is embedded in the **Plastic Waste Management Rules 2016 (amended 2022)**, **E-Waste (Management) Rules 2022** and **Battery Waste Management Rules 2022** — but was *first introduced* in the **e-Waste (Management and Handling) Rules, 2011**.

**Notebook.** GS3 — Environment (Pollution & waste management) with a GS3 Economy spillover on resource security.

**Static anchor.** Shankar IAS *Environment* — Pollution / Waste Management chapter. *Update:* add the 11 NITI focus sectors as a memorised list, and cross-link EPR to the three waste rules plus the 2019 PYQ.

articles.title: Acharya Vinoba Bhave's birth anniversary — the land-reform movement that worked morally and failed statistically — Modern History
articles.text:
**Headline:** The Prime Minister paid tribute to **Acharya Vinoba Bhave** on his **birth anniversary (11 September)** — born **Vinayak Narahari Bhave, 11 September 1895 – 15 November 1982** — the Gandhian who was hand-picked as India's **first individual Satyagrahi in 1940** and who launched the **Bhoodan movement in 1951**.

**Exam angle:** This is a **post-independence GS1 topic** that UPSC has asked in Mains verbatim (see the PYQ mirror), and the examinable argument is the gap between **moral success and structural failure**. Bhoodan was a **voluntary, non-legislative** alternative to state-led land redistribution: Bhave walked village to village asking landowners to gift land, and from **1954** escalated to **Gramdan**, the donation of whole villages into common ownership. The movement collected roughly **42 lakh acres**, but only a fraction was ever distributed — much of it was **litigated, uncultivable, or reverted** when Gramdan villages drifted back to individual title. The reason to know the numbers is that they let you make the argument precisely: voluntary transfer could not overcome **absentee landlordism, benami holdings and defective land records** — which is exactly the diagnosis that statutory **land-ceiling legislation** and, much later, **land-records digitisation** were meant to address. That gives you a live cross-link to **DILRMP 3.0** (12 September note). The second thread is **ideological**: Bhoodan is the practical arm of **Sarvodaya** and of Gandhi's **trusteeship** doctrine, and its political afterlife runs through **Jayaprakash Narayan**, who left party politics for Sarvodaya in 1954 and returned in 1974 with **Sampoorna Kranti** — a chain worth writing in one line.

**Facts to memorise:**

- **Vinayak Narahari "Vinoba" Bhave**, b. **11 September 1895**, Gagode village, **Raigad district, Maharashtra** (Konkan); d. 15 November 1982. Gandhi gave him the name **Vinoba**, placing him in the lineage of **Jnanoba and Tukoba**. Met Gandhi at **Ahmedabad, 7 June 1916**.
- **First individual Satyagrahi**, selected by Gandhi to launch the **Individual Civil Disobedience Movement, October 1940**; **Jawaharlal Nehru** was the second. Gandhi introduced him publicly through the essay ***"Who is Vinoba?"***
- **Bhoodan (land-gift) movement:** launched **18 April 1951** at **Pochampally village, Nalgonda district** (then Hyderabad State, now **Telangana**), where **Vedre Ramachandra Reddy** donated **100 acres** to landless Harijan families. **Gramdan** (village-gift) followed from **1954**; the first Gramdan village was **Mangroth (Uttar Pradesh)**.
- **Institutions:** **Sarva Seva Sangh** and the **Akhil Bharat Sarva Seva Sangh** carried the movement; **Gram Seva Mandal, Wardha (1934)**; earlier, the **Nagpur Flag Satyagraha (1923)**.
- **Writings:** ***Geetai*** (the Bhagavad Gita in Marathi verse, 1930–31); ***Gita Pravachane*** (18 talks delivered in **Dhule jail, 1932**); *Swarajya-Shastra*; *Sthitaprajna-Darshan*.
- **Honours:** first international **Ramon Magsaysay Award for Community Leadership (1958)**; **Bharat Ratna, posthumously in 1983**.
- **Contrast to hold ready:** Bhoodan = **voluntary and moral**; **land-ceiling laws** = **statutory and coercive**, and many were placed in the **Ninth Schedule** to shield them from judicial review.

**Notebook:** GS1 — Modern Indian History and post-independence consolidation (social reformers; land reforms), with a GS4 spillover (trusteeship, moral persuasion as an instrument of change).

**Static anchor:** **Spectrum / Bipan Chandra — the post-independence land-reforms section; NCERT Class XII *Politics in India Since Independence*, Ch. 3 ("Politics of Planned Development").** *Update:* build a single **land-reforms ladder** — *Zamindari abolition (1950s) → Tenancy reform → Bhoodan–Gramdan (1951/1954, voluntary) → Land-ceiling legislation + Ninth Schedule → Consolidation of holdings → DILRMP/SVAMITVA (records, 2008–)* — and mark against each whether it was **voluntary or statutory** and **why it under-delivered**. **Cross-link** to your **Ninth Schedule / *I.R. Coelho* (2007)** note in Laxmikanth and to the **DILRMP 3.0** entry from 12 September.

articles.title: Rani Avantibai Lodhi gets a statue in Lucknow — the 1857 revolt beyond the four famous names — Modern History
articles.text:
**Headline.** Defence Minister **Rajnath Singh**, with UP Chief Minister **Yogi Adityanath**, unveiled a statue of **Veerangana Rani Avantibai Lodhi** in **Lucknow on 30 August 2026**, drawing a line from the 1857 warrior queens to women officers who flew combat roles in Operation Sindoor.

**Exam angle.** UPSC's 1857 questions have moved steadily away from Delhi–Kanpur–Lucknow and toward **regional centres and their leaders** — exactly the space Avantibai occupies. Her case is also the textbook illustration of a **doctrine that is not the Doctrine of Lapse**: her husband died leaving **minor** heirs, so the Company did not annex Ramgarh outright — it placed the estate under the **Court of Wards** and installed *sarbarahkars* (superintendents), a mechanism used for minor or "incompetent" heirs. That is a distinction students routinely get wrong, and it is precisely the sort of thing a statement-based Prelims question exploits. Avantibai expelled the Company's administrators, called on cultivators to refuse British revenue demands, and coordinated with the **Gond ruler Raja Shankar Shah of Garha-Mandla** through the famous **bangle appeal** — glass bangles sent with letters to neighbouring chiefs and zamindars, taunting them to fight or accept the bangles. She won at the **Battle of Kheri** near Mandla against Deputy Commissioner Waddington in 1857, then shifted to guerrilla operations from the **Devhargarh** hills, and took her own life on **20 March 1858** at Sukhi-Talaiya rather than be captured. Her Mahakoshal base — Gond and farming country — is the entry point for the **tribal dimension of 1857**, which is separate from and usually more useful than the sepoy narrative.

**Facts to memorise.**

- **Maharani Avantibai Lodhi**, **16 August 1831 – 20 March 1858**; queen-regent of the estate of **Ramgarh** (present-day **Dindori and Mandla districts, Madhya Pradesh**); born at **Mankedi village, Seoni district**.
- Married **Raja Vikramaditya Singh of Ramgarh**; assumed regency for minor sons **Aman Singh** and **Sher Singh** when he was incapacitated.
- Mechanism of British seizure: **Court of Wards** with **sarbarahkars** — not the **Doctrine of Lapse** (which applied to rulers dying *without* a natural heir).
- Ally: **Raja Shankar Shah**, Gond ruler of **Garha-Mandla**, executed by the British at Jabalpur in **September 1857** along with his son **Raghunath Shah** (blown from a cannon).
- **The bangle appeal** — glass bangles sent with letters to neighbouring rulers and zamindars as a challenge to join the revolt.
- **Battle of Kheri** (near Mandla, late 1857) — roughly **4,000 troops** defeated the force under Deputy Commissioner **Waddington**.
- Retreat to the **Devhargarh** hills; guerrilla strikes; encircled at **Sukhi-Talaiya** between Balapur and Ramgarh; **martyrdom on 20 March 1858**, aged 27.
- Group her with the other *veeranganas*: **Rani Lakshmibai (Jhansi)**, **Jhalkari Bai** (Lakshmibai's Durga Dal commander), **Begum Hazrat Mahal (Awadh)**, **Rani Durgavati** (16th-century Gond queen of Garha-Katanga — *not* 1857; a standard trap), **Uda Devi (Sikandar Bagh)**.
- Other 1857 centre-and-leader pairs to have cold: **Delhi — Bahadur Shah II / Bakht Khan; Kanpur — Nana Saheb / Tantia Tope; Lucknow — Begum Hazrat Mahal; Jhansi — Rani Lakshmibai; Bareilly — Khan Bahadur Khan; Bihar (Jagdishpur) — Kunwar Singh; Faizabad — Maulvi Ahmadullah Shah; Allahabad — Liaquat Ali; Assam — Kandarpeshwar Singha; Orissa (Sambalpur) — Surendra Sai.**

**Notebook:** GS1 — Modern History (the Revolt of 1857; significant personalities), with a GS1 Society cross-tag on women's participation in the freedom struggle.

**Static anchor:** **Spectrum — *A Brief History of Modern India*, "The Revolt of 1857"** chapter, plus the "Peasant and Tribal Uprisings" chapter for the Mahakoshal/Gond link. *Nudge: your 1857 centre-leader table almost certainly has six or seven rows. Extend it to twelve — add Ramgarh (Avantibai Lodhi), Garha-Mandla (Shankar Shah), Sambalpur (Surendra Sai), Faizabad (Maulvi Ahmadullah Shah) and Assam (Kandarpeshwar Singha) — and add a two-line box distinguishing the Doctrine of Lapse from the Court of Wards, since Ramgarh is a Court of Wards case, not a Lapse case.*

articles.title: Parliament passes the Bankers' Books Evidence Bill, 2026 — a 135-year-old colonial statute goes — Economy
articles.text:
**Headline:** The Rajya Sabha cleared the Bankers' Books Evidence Bill, 2026 on **10 August 2026** (Lok Sabha had passed it on 5 August), completing Parliamentary passage of a law that repeals and replaces the **Bankers' Books Evidence Act, 1891** and gives cloud-stored and digital bank records full evidentiary standing.

**Exam angle:** A quiet but genuinely high-yield item — it sits at the junction of GS3 Economy (banking, digital financial infrastructure) and GS2 (colonial-law repeal, ease of doing business). The larger story is India's evidence law catching up with a banking system where the "book" no longer exists physically: read it alongside the **Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023**, which already made electronic records admissible as *primary* evidence. Also a good Mains line on cutting litigation cost — banks no longer have to produce or prove physical ledgers in recovery and fraud proceedings, which matters for **DRTs, IBC proceedings and cyber-fraud prosecutions**.

**Facts to memorise:**

- Bill No. **147 of 2026**; introduced in Lok Sabha **3 August 2026**, passed LS **5 August**, passed RS **10 August 2026**. Repeals the **Bankers' Books Evidence Act, 1891**.
- **"Bankers' books" redefined** to cover ledgers, day-books, cash-books, account books and all records used in ordinary banking business, kept in **physical, electronic, digital or cloud-based** form — including **back-up and disaster-recovery sites**, onsite or offsite/virtual.
- Electronic/digital records are **admissible, valid and legally enforceable** subject to conditions: the system was in regular use and operating properly, no unauthorised alteration or tampering, and the network/devices were secured against cyber risk.
- **"Legal proceeding" widened** to include court proceedings, **arbitration**, and investigations/inquiries conducted under law for collection of evidence.
- **Retained safeguard:** a bank officer cannot be compelled to produce a banker's book, or appear as a witness to prove its contents, in a proceeding to which the bank is **not a party** — except by order of a court or judge made **for a special cause**.

**Notebook:** GS3 — Economy (Banking & Financial Sector Reform); cross-file in GS2 (Repeal of colonial laws)

**Static anchor:** **Mrunal — Pillar 3 (Banking / BFSI)**, banking-regulation sub-section. Add a short "evidence & recovery architecture" box, and **cross-link** it to your Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 note on Sections 61–63 (electronic records as primary evidence) so the two laws sit on one page.

articles.title: Hyderabad hosts the 2nd BRICS Anti-Corruption Working Group and Asset Recovery Expert Network — International Relations
articles.text:
**Headline:** The Department of Personnel and Training is hosting the second meeting of the **BRICS Anti-Corruption Working Group (ACWG)** and the second meeting of the **BRICS Expert Network on Asset Recovery** in Hyderabad on **4–5 August 2026**, under India's BRICS Chairship of 2026. Inauguration by DoPT Secretary Ms Rachna Shah.

**Exam angle:**
- India's BRICS Chairship year is a guaranteed GS2/IR theme; the examinable distinction is **which ministry is nodal for which BRICS track** — DoPT for anti-corruption, unlike the more familiar MEA/Finance-led tracks.
- This is the "economic-offender extradition and asset recovery" theme that UPSC likes to pair with **UNCAC (2003)**, the **Fugitive Economic Offenders Act, 2018**, and Mutual Legal Assistance Treaties. Note the agenda language: cooperation is **"informal"** — i.e. agency-to-agency channels that run *alongside*, not in place of, formal MLAT/extradition routes.
- The FinTech and digital-asset corruption-risk agenda is a fresh GS3 crossover (crypto, virtual digital assets, PMLA reporting entity obligations).

**Key facts / figures to memorise:**
- Theme of India's BRICS Chairship 2026: **"Building for Resilience, Innovation, Cooperation and Sustainability"**.
- Nodal department for the BRICS anti-corruption track in India: **DoPT, Ministry of Personnel, Public Grievances and Pensions**.
- Three agenda pillars: (i) informal cooperation to **trace fugitive offenders** and support extradition; (ii) operational information-sharing through the **Expert Network on Asset Recovery**; (iii) corruption risks from **FinTech, digital assets and emerging digital financial instruments**.
- Side event on 5 August: **"Ethical Governance through Innovation and Tech-Driven Systems"** — digital public procurement, citizen engagement, transparency.
- Anchor treaty: **UN Convention against Corruption (UNCAC), 2003** — India signed in 2005, ratified in **2011**.

**Destination notebook:** GS2 — International Relations (Groupings & Agreements involving India); cross-file under GS4/GS2 Governance (probity, transparency).

**Static anchor:** *Laxmikanth* — chapters on the **CVC** and the **Lokpal and Lokayuktas**, plus your BRICS institutional note. **Update:** add a "BRICS working-group architecture under India's 2026 Chairship" line to the BRICS page, and cross-link the **Prevention of Corruption Act, 1988 (as amended 2018)** and the **Fugitive Economic Offenders Act, 2018** from the anti-corruption page.

articles.title: Second meeting of the BRICS Anti-Corruption Working Group opens in Hyderabad
articles.text:
**Ministry:** Personnel, Public Grievances and Pensions (DoPT) | **Date:** 04 Aug 2026

The **2nd meeting of the BRICS Anti-Corruption Working Group (ACWG)** began in **Hyderabad on 4–5 August 2026**, held alongside the **2nd meeting of the BRICS Expert Network on Asset Recovery**. **Ms. Rachna Shah, Secretary, DoPT**, was chief guest; **Shri J. articles.title: Rakhigarhi skeletons transferred to AnSI for ancient-DNA study
articles.text:
**Headline:** ASI formally handed Harappan skeletal remains from **Rakhigarhi (Haryana)** to the **Anthropological Survey of India (AnSI)** for advanced research.

**Exam angle (GS1 — Art & Culture/Ancient History):** Reinforces "Places in News" + Harappan civilisation + India's growing **ancient-DNA/bioarchaeology** capacity. Two premier Ministry of Culture bodies (ASI ↔ AnSI) under an MoU.

**Memorise:** Rakhigarhi = among the **largest Indus–Saraswati (Harappan)** settlements, in Haryana (Ghaggar plain). 2025–26 field season (ASI Excavation Branch-II) found **8 burials at Mound No. 7**; **3 complete skeletons** + fragments moved to AnSI's skeletal repository, **Kolkata**. Aim: ancestry, diet, health, migration via aDNA.

**Notebook:** GS1 — Ancient History / Art & Culture. **Static anchor:** Old NCERT *"Bricks, Beads and Bones"* / Nitin Singhania IVC chapter — add Rakhigarhi (largest site) and the AnSI ancient-DNA link.
